title: Unification of Germany and Italy: Making Nations in the 19th Century

questions.question: Bismarck's famous 'Blood and Iron' speech argued that Germany would be unified by:
options: War and military power, not speeches and votes
questions.rationale: Bismarck told the Prussian Landtag in 1862 that the great questions of the day are decided by iron and blood - a top-down, conservative unification through three engineered wars (1864, 1866, 1870-71).

questions.question: The German Empire was proclaimed in 1871 at:
questions.rationale: Wilhelm I was proclaimed Kaiser in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles - a deliberate humiliation of defeated France, whose loss of Alsace-Lorraine then fed revanche for two generations.

questions.question: The Zollverein (1834) contributed to German unification by:
options: Economically integrating the German states under Prussian leadership
questions.rationale: The customs union knitted 39 states into one market with Prussia at the centre - economic union preceding and smoothing political union, while Austria, excluded, watched its influence bleed away.

questions.question: The Austro-Prussian War of 1866 resulted in:
questions.rationale: The Seven Weeks' War ended at Koniggratz with Austria crushed and pushed out of German politics; the North German Confederation followed in 1867 under Prussian leadership.

questions.question: Who founded the secret society Young Italy in 1831?
questions.rationale: Mazzini was the movement's prophet - republican, romantic, insurrectionary. Cavour was the pragmatic statesman, Garibaldi the soldier, Victor Emmanuel the king who reaped what the other three sowed.

questions.question: The Pact of Plombieres (1858) was an agreement between Piedmont and:
questions.rationale: Cavour secretly agreed with Napoleon III that France would help expel Austria from northern Italy in exchange for Nice and Savoy. It produced the war of 1859 - Magenta and Solferino - and brought Lombardy to Piedmont.

questions.question: Garibaldi's Expedition of the Thousand (1860) began with the landing at:
questions.rationale: The red-shirted Mille landed at Marsala in May 1860, took Sicily and then crossed to the mainland to conquer Naples - handing the south to King Victor Emmanuel II at Teano rather than founding a republic.

questions.question: Rome became the capital of unified Italy in 1871 because:
options: The French garrison left to fight Prussia in 1870
The Pope invited the king in
questions.rationale: Napoleon III's protection of the Pope ended when France fell to Prussia in 1870; Italian troops entered Rome through the Porta Pia breach, completing the kingdom. The Pope declared himself the 'prisoner of the Vatican' until Mussolini's Lateran Pacts of 1929.

questions.question: German unification is best described as:
options: A top-down, Prussian-led unification without Austria
A federation of equals with Austria included
questions.rationale: Kleindeutsch: Prussia annexed and absorbed the northern states after 1866 and rode nationalist fervour against France in 1870-71 to weld the south in - monarchy and army, not parliament, made Germany.

questions.question: The Frankfurt Parliament of 1848 was significant because it:
options: Tried and failed to unify Germany through liberal debate
questions.rationale: The all-German assembly offered the crown to Frederick William IV, who refused it from the gutter - proving (to Bismarck's generation) that speeches and majorities would not make a nation; armies would.
